text:
ajay: quick ask — can someone validate perf parity for private/VPC vs hosted for our on‑prem build 1.3.2? Customer lab run shows ~1.8x p95 tail latency regression. Need p95, throughput (tokens/s), GPU/CPU util and any env diffs. link: https://redwood.internal/runs/1234 :eyes:

sam: which model + exact runtime config? hosted baseline we use redwood-4x-quant, batch=4, seq=512, fp16/q8x. image for hosted is rwd/inference:hosted-1.3.2.

ajay: same model + quant. on‑prem image is rwd/inference:private-1.3.2, kernel 5.15 vs hosted 5.18. suspect NIC offloads / nv_peer_mem / pci settings. also saw lower GPU util in the lab run.

caroline: i'll spin up the bench on rack7 (lab7) and run the harness. ETA ~30m. tagging @sam for config parity checks.

caroline: running now — command i'm using:```bash
rwd-bench --model redwood-4x-quant --image rwd/inference:private-1.3.2 --seq 512 --batch 4 --iters 200 --measure p95,throughput --export /tmp/run-private-1234.json
```

caroline: initial results pasted (lab7, before tuning):
```
p95 = 112ms (hosted baseline = 62ms)
throughput = 980 tokens/s (hosted = 1600 tokens/s)
GPU util = 40% (hosted = 78%)
CPU steal = 3%
net retransmits + slightly higher latency on TCP
```

sam: ouch. first checks: confirm nvidia drivers + nvidia-container-runtime versions match, NCCL version, GPU clock governor (performance), and PCIe gen. also confirm runtime config: `io_mode`, `max_batch_latency_ms`, cgroup cpuset. any cgroup throttling?

marco: also check kernel offloads — SLES vs Ubuntu have different default NIC offload settings. NVLINK/peer mem modules matter for multi‑GPU tight loops. search for `nv_peer_mem` in /etc/modules-load.d/.

caroline: found missing nv_peer_mem load in the image and a diff in `/etc/security/limits.d/` (nofile lower). re-enabled nv_peer_mem and bumped GPU clocks to performance. re-ran:
```
p95 = 68ms
throughput = 1480 tokens/s
GPU util = 72%
```

ajay: that's a huge improvement, thanks. remaining gap small (68ms vs 62ms). can we capture perf counters (SM cycles, memory bw) and compare? also check host kernel version and nic driver (hosted is kernel 5.18 + igb_uio tuning).

sam: i'll pull perf metrics from the hosted baseline and grab the exact runtime config we're running in prod. also will diff docker run flags (capabilities, net=host, cpu pinning).

caroline: added the run output + exact bench script to the run artifact at https://redwood.internal/artifacts/run-private-1234.json. infra-ci: quick smoke?

infra-ci: smoke tests and basic healthchecks passed for the run image. :white_check_mark:

marco: small note — our onprem racks have 100Gb NICs but MTU was 1500, hosted uses jumbo MTU 9000 which reduces segmentation overhead for big KV transfers. enabling jumbo on the switch + hosts dropped a few ms on our cluster tests.

ajay: good catch. can someone create a tiny parity checklist and a PR to the ops-runbook with the gating test command + expected ranges? we should gate private images to not regress >1.2x hosted p95.

sam: will open PR with bench script + gating thresholds. tagging @caroline to attach the run artifact. :thumbsup:

caroline: done — PR #842 opened with config + results, CI bench added to nightly perf job. link: https://redwood.internal/pr/842

ajay: perfect. next steps: 1) merge PR, 2) add kernel/NIC checks to onboarding script for private installs, 3) follow up on remaining 6ms gap (likely minor kernel/driver tunables). thanks all. :raised_hands:
